items.headline: Are We Losing Control of AI? What’s Driving New Fears
items.summary: For years, as artificial intelligence has evolved from the stuff of sci-fi movies to an app ordinary people have installed on their phones, tech leaders and some AI insiders have talked about the potential for it to escape human control and wreak havoc on society. Those fears have become impossible to ignore in recent days, driven by advances in the technology, a series of cybersecurity breaches involving AI agents, and new warnings from rank-and-file AI staffers.
items.author: William Norris, Nilushi Karunaratne and Thomas Pfeiffer

items.headline: Trump’s AI Defense Defies Voter Unease Heading Into Midterms
items.summary: President Donald Trump’s opposition to guardrails on artificial intelligence puts him at odds with a growing number of lawmakers from both parties, with AI safety fears adding to voters’ misgivings about the technology heading into the midterm elections.
items.author: Michael Shepard, Erik Wasson and Hadriana Lowenkron

items.headline: Meta Bulls Bet Stock Will Break Out After Year of Head Fakes
items.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. shares have been on a rollercoaster ride through 2026, rising and falling as investor belief in the Facebook parent’s status as a player in the artificial intelligence space ebbs and flows.
items.author: Ryan Vlastelica

items.headline: Intel-Backed Chipmaker Altera Files Confidentially for IPO
items.summary: Altera, a chipmaker backed by Silver Lake and Intel Corp., filed confidentially for an initial public offering.
items.author: David Morris

items.headline: Why Are Tesla and SpaceX Separate? Musk Says ‘Great Question’
items.summary: Elon Musk again teased the idea of his AI and rocket firm SpaceX combining with electric-car maker Tesla Inc., noting the extensive cooperation between the two companies he leads as chief executive officer.
items.author: Loren Grush

items.headline: An AI Pause Won’t Work Without China
items.summary: A simulated AI-created WeChat bug shows why slowing the AI race won't work without global cooperation. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Catherine Thorbecke says the US and China need to make transparency on AI risks a priority. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Meta Touts the Cost-Saving Benefits of Latest In-House AI Chips
items.summary: New processor will be running in data centers next year, with another model to follow by end of 2027
items.author: Dina Bass

items.headline: Carlyle’s Fujiyama Sees Investor Excitement in Defense Tech
items.summary: Carlyle Global Head of Aerospace, Defense and Government Ian Fujiyama spoke with Bloomberg’s Dani Burger from the sidelines of Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference in Washington. He discussed the wave of investor excitement in defense tech, investing at the edge of innovation, supply-chain resilience, AI in defense, and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: OpenAI Says It’s Working With Anthropic, Google on AI Safety
items.summary: OpenAI is working on steps to address artificial intelligence safety issues with its top competitors Anthropic PBC and Google DeepMind, escalating industry efforts to respond to a groundswell of concern that the technology poses an economic and security threat.
items.author: Maggie Eastland

items.headline: Coinbase Slides Ahead of Clarity Act Vote; Waystar Up on Sale Exploration | Stock Movers
items.summary: On this episode of Stock Movers: - Dave & Buster's (PLAY) shares are lower after it reported revenue for the second quarter that missed the average analyst estimate. - Coinbase (COIN) along with other crypto shares along with Bitcoin are sliding ahead of the Senate's vote on the CLARITY Act that would regulate digital assets and the crypto industry. - Waystar (WAY) shares are higher after Reuters reported that the firm is exploring options, including a sale, two years after a public listing in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Carlyle’s Chi Says Credit Portfolios Remain Resilient
items.summary: Carlyle Deputy CIO of Global Credit and Head of Direct Lending Alex Chi spoke with Bloomberg’s Dani Burger from the sidelines of Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference in Washington. He talked about resilience in credit portfolios, where Carlyle sees the best opportunities in credit, AI’s impact on credit markets, and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Carlyle’s Redett on Navigating Fundraising Supercycle
items.summary: Carlyle Co-President and Head of Global Private Equity John Redett spoke with Bloomberg’s Dani Burger from the sidelines of Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference in Washington. He talked about current investment opportunities, AI across the portfolio, higher-for-longer rates and private equity, and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Attorney General Blanche Opposes AI ‘Regulation by Prosecution’
items.summary: US Attorney General Todd Blanche says he prefers a restrained approach to taking enforcement action against artificial intelligence companies and executives amid a rising debate over the risks of the cutting-edge technology.
items.author: Chris Strohm and Leah Nylen

items.headline: Should AI Development Slow Down? Inside the Debate: Live Q&A
items.summary: Bloomberg journalists answer your questions about the high-stakes debate over calls to slow down AI development ahead of the US midterm elections in a Live Q&A today at 2:30 p.m. EDT
items.author: Seth Fiegerman, Edward Ludlow, Maggie Eastland and Jordan Robertson

items.headline: Nvidia CEO Puts Trump on Phone While Downplaying AI Risk
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang took a live phone call from Donald Trump during a panel discussion, allowing the US president to dismiss artificial intelligence dangers as a “hoax." Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Carlyle’s Basmadjian on AI Debt Reshaping the Loan Market
items.summary: Carlyle Global Head of Liquid Credit Lauren Basmadjian spoke with Bloomberg’s Dani Burger from the sidelines of Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference and talked about the health of corporate borrowers, the loan market moving toward equilibrium, data centers as an emerging source of loan supply, and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Amazon Fails to Recover Some Data in Facilities Hit in Iran War
items.summary: Amazon.com Inc. has been unable to restore access to some of the data stored at Persian Gulf facilities damaged during the US-Iran war.
items.author: Matt Day

items.headline: Inside Carlyle's Global Investment Conference, Bessent Faces Big Questions
items.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger and Isabelle Lee on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Dani Burger is at Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference, talking defense tech, AI and the outlook for credit with Ian Fujiyama, Jason Thomas and Alex Chi. Plus, the Fed under pressure, questions over an AI slowdown and Scott Bessent in the Capitol Hill spotlight on inflation, energy and AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: OpenAI Eyes Canada Data Center Partnerships at Carney Investment Summit
items.summary: OpenAI Inc. is taking a close look at Canada under Prime Minister Mark Carney, said one of its top executives who previously hired the Canadian to lead the Bank of England.
items.author: Thomas Seal

items.headline: Apple AirPods 5 Offer Noise Cancellation, Sound Improvements at $129 Price
items.summary: It’s worth spending an extra $20 for wireless charging and volume controls, but both versions of the AirPods 5 offer improved sound and noise cancellation.
items.author: Chris Welch
